subject: Intermittent truncation on long-context streaming during BrightLane demo
messages:
From: Sam Torres <sam@brightlane.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: engineering@brightlane.ai
Date: 2027-12-11T08:13:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SDK during long-doc demo — truncated outputs

Marissa,

During today's internal demo of BrightLane's legal-doc summarizer (we feed ~40k chars), we saw the Redwood streaming response cut off at ~2.4k tokens twice in the same session. The final event shows a client-side EOF but no server 5xx.

We collected client logs and captured a session trace. Attaching a tar with logs and a JSON trace. Can your team help confirm whether this is a client-side streaming timeout or a runtime truncation? The behavior is intermittent — happens ~2/10 runs, usually after ~120s.

Quick ask: can we get an RCA window / whether a canary fix is possible before our customer demo next week?

Thanks,
Sam Torres
Staff ML Eng, BrightLane

From: logan_wright@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-11T10:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SDK during long-doc demo — truncated outputs

Marissa / team — I pulled the session id from the attached trace (session: brt-20271211-44). Quick notes from an initial runtime check:

- No 5xx recorded on the serving host for that session id; CPU and GPU were healthy.
- I do see an open connection that drops after ~123s with the server yielding a final chunk size smaller than expected (partial EOS).
- Runtime logs show an internal streaming flush when KV-cache exceeded configured soft limit for a worker (we have an opportunistic flush path that can cause early termination for very long prefix caches). That path is supposed to trigger only when memory pressure is high; here memory looked nominal but we did hit a large KV windows allocation.

Hypothesis: the runtime flush path may be racing with the streaming write, producing a truncated final chunk without an explicit error code. If this is right, mitigation could be a config flip to disable opportunistic flush for specific worker pools or a small patch to ensure EOF is sent to the streaming socket before flush.

Requests:
- Dev: can you share the SDK client keepalive / idle-timeout settings used in BrightLane's trace? Their trace shows long gaps between heartbeats.
- Marissa: Sam — can you confirm whether they used the default SDK (v2.1.0) or a custom client?

I'll start a focused debug on the worker where that session landed and try to repro with an artificial long prefix.

—Logan
Runtime Eng Lead
From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: logan_wright@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-11T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SDK during long-doc demo — truncated outputs

Logan / Marissa — thanks for the heads up. I've pulled the client logs in brightlane_sdk_logs.tar.gz. Key findings:

- BrightLane is on SDK v2.1.0 with a custom connect wrapper that increases socket timeout to 180s but does not send intermediate pings; the SDK defaults to a 60s HTTP/2 ping interval unless overridden.
- The session trace shows the client did not send periodic pings for the long generation; there are ~70s gaps where the server won't get a keepalive.

Repro plan I'm attaching: session_trace_20271211.json has a minimal reproducer that I ran locally with the same payload; I can reproduce a truncated final chunk when I force the worker to do an opportunistic KV flush. I'll open a small SDK fix to make our default keepalive behavior explicit (send a ping every 30s during streaming) and add a telemetry flag to surface intermediate write failures.

Temporary mitigation: recommend BrightLane set their wrapper to send periodic pings or set the SDK socket option keepalive to true; I'll share a short patch and a config snippet they can apply in their staging tomorrow.

Attaching: session_trace_20271211.json (reproducer).

—Dev Patel
Software Engineer, SDK
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Sam Torres <sam@brightlane.ai>
Cc: logan_wright@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-12T15:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SDK during long-doc demo — truncated outputs

Sam — quick status and next steps: thanks for the trace and logs, that sped things up. Summary:

- Cause (interim): combination of long client gaps without pings + a runtime opportunistic KV-cache flush racing with the final stream write produced a truncated final chunk without an explicit server error.
- Immediate mitigation (today): Dev sent a small SDK snippet BrightLane can drop into their wrapper to send pings every 30s; we recommend enabling socket keepalive.
- Short-term fix (this sprint): Logan's runtime team will flip the opportunistic flush toggle for the worker pool that BrightLane hit and add a guard to ensure EOF is emitted before internal cache eviction. Target: canary by 2027-12-16.
- Long-term: add better telemetry to surface partial-stream writes and update SDK doc defaults for long streaming workloads.

Action items:
- marissa_cole: share the SDK snippet and instructions (done; sent via Drive link).
- dev_patel: open SDK PR with keepalive default + telemetry flag (PR: #2984).
- logan_wright: runtime canary and guard (ETA: 2027-12-16).
- sam / brightlane: apply SDK snippet to staging and confirm tomorrow morning demo run.

Sam — can you confirm you got the snippet and whether staging confirms the mitigation? If yes we'll mark this resolved on the deal and record the RCA in the postmortem doc.

Thanks everyone — great cross-team response.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
